mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% consistently precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as low interest rates reduce discount rates for equity cash flows and encourage risk-taking in equity markets.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.5% signals accelerating inflation, prompting Federal Reserve tightening expectations that cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL MoM increase exceeds 0.5% (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous month-over-month increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% indicate robust consumer demand, driving corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 0.5% MoM and RSAFS rises > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS rise > 0.5% MoM (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), tight labor markets drive wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 1.0% signals economic contraction, reducing corporate earnings expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO MoM decline exceeds 1.0% (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) above 100 (2017 base) consistently correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, reflecting a functioning industrial sector that supports corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO > 100 (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous month-over-month growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.1 percentage points indicate labor market strengthening, boosting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp MoM
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS rises > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp MoM (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.5%), elevated valuations and anticipated monetary tightening cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.5% (over 5-year rolling window).
